FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: risi e bisi
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} and {1_coll} cooked together, somewhere between a soup and a risotto — loose enough for the spoon, too thick for the bowl. The pods go into the stock; nothing is wasted.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: gnocchi
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} crushed while still hot and bound with as little flour as can be managed, rolled, and ridged with a fork. They are done when they rise.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: osso buco
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: slices of shin braised in {1_plur} and {2_plur}, the bone left in the middle. The marrow it holds is the whole reason for the dish.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: {0_adj} parmigiana
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} sliced, drawn in salt and then fried, built up in layers with {1_plur} and {2_plur}, and browned. The salt takes out the bitterness; without it the dish cannot be eaten.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: caponata
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} fried apart, brought together with {1_plur} melted down and {2_plur}, then made sweet-and-sour with vinegar and sugar. Eaten cold, the next day, once the acidity has settled.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: minestrone
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a soup out of the back of the larder: {0_coll}, {1_coll} and {2_coll} stewed with no fixed recipe. Better the next day, which suits everybody.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: ribollita
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: literally reboiled: yesterday's {0_adj} and {1_adj} soup, thickened with stale bread and put back on the heat until it will no longer run.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: panna cotta
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} barely warmed with {1_plur}, set in the cold just enough to hold, and napped with a {2_adj} coulis. It has to tremble when the plate is set down.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: cannoli
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: tubes of pastry fried around a cane, filled with sweetened {1_plur} and {2_plur} at the last moment. Filled in advance they go soft and are worth nothing.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: focaccia
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a very wet dough dimpled with the fingertips, drowned in {1_adj} oil and salted in coarse grains. The holes hold the oil: they are not decorative.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: arancini
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: cold leftover risotto packed into a ball around a {2_adj} heart, rolled in a {1_adj} crumb and fried. The name means little oranges, after the colour they take coming out of the oil.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: caprese
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} and {1_coll} in alternating slices, oil, salt, green leaves. Nothing else, and above all no vinegar.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: saltimbocca
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: an escalope of {0_adj} flattened out, a sage leaf and a slice of {1_adj} pinned to it, seared a minute a side. The name says: leaps into the mouth.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: vitello tonnato
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} poached, cooled, sliced as thin as it will go, and napped with a cold {1_adj} sauce mounted with {2_plur}. The pairing seems absurd until the first mouthful.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: panzanella
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: hard bread soaked and then pressed out, mixed with {1_plur} and {2_plur}. A dish invented to throw nothing away, and now a dish people ask for.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: bagna càuda
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} melted down in {2_plur} with a great deal of {1_adj}, kept warm over a flame. Raw vegetables are dipped into it; the smell stays in the room for three days.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: fritto misto
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} rolled in flour, thrown into scalding oil and lifted straight back out, served with {2_plur}. Eaten standing, out of paper, before it has cooled.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: polpette
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} minced and lightened with soaked crumb, rolled into balls and finished in a {2_adj} sauce.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: cotoletta alla milanese
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a {0_adj} chop left on its bone, taken through {2_plur} and then breadcrumbs, and cooked in clarified butter. Milan and Vienna have argued over which came first for two centuries.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: amatriciana
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {2_coll} rendered slowly until it turns translucent, {1_coll} added to the fat it gives up, and the pasta finished in it.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: zabaione
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: the yolks of {0_adj} whisked with {1_plur} and {2_plur} over a water bath, until they treble in volume. One second too long and it is a sweet omelette.
